_nota: Scheda 'Come funziona' della guida: spiega solo come si usa ogni strumento della piattaforma, mai dove sta la risposta di un esercizio.

punti: It's the Cinque Foglie website as a customer sees it: the menu at the top leads to the categories, the cards to the products.
The dark Inspect button, next to the address, shows the data Google reads: status, title, description, meta robots, canonical and H1.
If you open an address that has a redirect, a notice at the top explains it.
Changes saved in the Shop admin show up here straight away.
It lists all the website's addresses, the way Google finds them by following links. Under each address, in grey, is its title.
On the left the filters group the problems into Errors, To fix and To check. The number next to each says how many pages there are.
The Filter addresses box searches within the filter you've chosen.
Click a row to open the Address details, below the table: there you'll find all the page's data, the notes and where it's linked from.
The table scrolls horizontally. Rows you've changed in the admin have an orange line.
At the top choose the part of the website, the period and whether to compare with the year before: the chart and the numbers change.
The Queries tab (what people search for) and the Pages tab (the website's pages) show clicks, impressions, CTR and position.
Click a column header to sort. Click a query to see which pages of the website appear for that search.
URL inspection: type an address to compare what Google remembers with today's website. From there you can request indexing.
Two tabs: Page indexing and Core Web Vitals (speed).
The chart shows, week by week, the pages on Google (green) and those left out (grey). Below are the marked events.
The table of reasons explains why some pages are left out. Click a reason to see the pages, the On the website today column and the Validate fix button.
Core Web Vitals splits pages into groups and shows the timings on phone and on computer, with the main cause.
Type in the box to search the keywords.
Columns: Intent (what the searcher wants), Volume (searches per month), Difficulty, Trend (one small bar per month, from July to June) and Website position.
Only where the website doesn't appear shows the keywords we're not in the results for.
The table scrolls horizontally; click a column header to sort.
They show what happens after the click on Google: visits, orders and revenue.
The table has one row per landing page: Sessions, Conversion (out of 100 visits, how many become an order), Orders and Revenue.
The chart shows revenue from Google month by month.
You can filter the pages and sort by clicking the column headers.
It's the website's back office, like WordPress or Shopify. It has three tabs: Pages, Redirects and Theme and settings.
Pages: choose a page from the list (or search for it) and change title, description, H1, text and meta robots. The Google preview updates as you type. Then press Save changes.
Redirects: write From (old address) and To (new page) and press Save the 301. In the table you can edit or delete.
Theme and settings: which categories are visible to search engines and the canonical of filtered pages.
Every change goes live straight away. Back to the original undoes the changes to a page.
Write the requested text here. It saves itself in this browser.
Press Check my work: the guide says what's fine and what's missing. You can try again as many times as you like.
It's the Cinque Foglie profile as followers see it: the bio at the top, the grid of posts below.
Click a post to open it: you'll see the caption, publishing date and time, alt text and any partnership label.
In the open post you can edit the caption, alt text and label, or archive it (it disappears from the profile but isn't deleted).
At the top, the numbers for the period and the follower trend.
The Active followers by hour chart says what time followers are online.
The table has one row per post: reach, impressions, interactions, saves, engagement rate. Click a column header to sort.
The filters above the table show only one format or one pillar.
The Averages by format box compares reels, carousels and photos.
On the left the drafts; in the middle the calendar with scheduled posts. You can change month with the arrows.
Drag a draft onto a day to schedule it (or open it and choose date and time).
Click a post or a draft to open the editor: format, caption, alt text, link, date and time. Then Save.
Scheduling settings holds the time used when scheduling several posts in bulk.
Comments on posts and private messages arrive here, most recent first.
On each item you can reply, hide (it stays visible only to the person who wrote it), report as spam or hand it over to a colleague.
The filters at the top show only unanswered comments or only messages.
It collects photos, videos and music the team can use.
Each item says where it comes from and what permission or licence it has.
For other people's photos you can write the message to ask for permission here.
The table lists the campaigns with October's numbers: impressions, clicks, CTR, cost, conversions, CPA, ROAS and impressions lost to budget. Click a column header to sort.
Click a campaign's name to open it: at the top the daily budget and status (with Save), then the negative keywords and the ad groups.
In each group: the keywords table (change the match type from the row's menu; click the Quality score to see its three parts), the Add keyword form and the ad with the Edit the ad button.
In the ad: up to 15 headlines (30 characters) and 4 descriptions (90 characters), with the counter beside them, the final URL and, if needed, the end date.
They show what people actually typed before clicking an ad, with the keyword that made it appear.
Filter by campaign or keyword with the menus at the top; click a column header to sort.
The Exclude button on a row lets you choose which words to add as the campaign's negatives. Negatives already added are listed above the table.
Keyword ideas with searches per month, the expected cost per click (from… to…), competition and intent (purchase, informational or mixed).
Type in the box to search; click a column header to sort.
The planner doesn't add anything to campaigns: keywords are added from the Campaigns.
What happens after the click, group by group: landing page, sessions, bounce rate (people who leave straight away), orders and revenue.
Next to them are the ad cost and the group's ROAS, for comparison.
At the top, the products' average gross margin: it tells you when a campaign makes money.
At the top the Tagline and the Positioning: fields to fill in, with the Save button.
Below, to read: mission, values, tone of voice (what we are, what we aren't, rules and before-and-after examples), logo and colours.

It collects the data on the brand: customer segments, competitors, NPS month by month with the detractors' reasons, shipping times, searches for the name over the last two years and the awareness survey.
At the bottom, the quality office's sheet on packaging: the verified facts.
Each section says where the data comes from.
Six brand texts on different channels (website, email, social media, customer service, packaging).
On each text: Edit, write the new version and press Save. Back to the original undoes it.
The counter under the text says how many words and characters it has.
A page with five parts: goal, audience, key message, channels and KPIs.
Goal, audience and message are written; channels and KPIs are chosen from the boxes.
Press Save the plan to save it.

Three tabs: Press release (headline, subheading, text, contacts, with the word counter), Journalists (choose who to send it to, read the notes) and Requests (journalists' questions, with the form to reply).
Next to them are the facts on the calendar and the internal note on the kits: use only verified information.
In a text, an empty line separates paragraphs.
